title: How Much Does a Kids' Birthday Party Cost in Singapore? (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: A clear 2026 breakdown of kids' birthday party costs in Singapore — from budget home parties to premium celebrations — plus what drives the price and how to save.
excerpt: What a children's party really costs in Singapore in 2026 — realistic ranges, what drives the price, and where to save without cutting the joy.
dek: One of the first questions every parent asks — and the honest answer is 'it depends'. Here's a realistic breakdown for Singapore in 2026, so you can budget with confidence.

sections.html: Most styled children's birthday parties in Singapore land somewhere between $300 and $2,500, depending on guest numbers, venue and how much you'd like done for you. A simple at-home celebration with balloons and a cake can cost a few hundred dollars; a fully styled party with décor, entertainment, catering and photography sits higher. The good news: you can dial the spend up or down at almost every step.

Four things move the number more than anything else:

  • Guest count — more children means more catering, more party favours and often a bigger space.
  • Venue — a party at home or a condo function room is far cheaper than a restaurant or dedicated venue.
  • Décor — balloon styling ranges from a simple garland to a full backdrop installation.
  • Extras — entertainment, a custom cake, catering and photography each add to the total but also lift the day.

Cosy (from ~$300–$600): at home or a function room, a balloon garland, a lovely cake, and a simple grazing spread you top up yourself.

Mid-range (~$700–$1,500): a styled backdrop, custom cake and dessert table, light catering, and one entertainment act such as a magician or face painter.

Premium (~$1,500–$2,500+): a full styled setup, catering for adults and children, a headline entertainer, and a photographer to capture it all.

sections.h2: How to save without losing the magic
sections.html:
• Choose a condo function room — often the single biggest saving.
  • Invest in one statement element (usually the backdrop) rather than spreading thin across many.
  • Keep the guest list tight for younger children — toddlers do beautifully in small groups.
  • Let one concierge coordinate everything, so you're not paying for overlaps or last-minute premiums.

We build a package around your budget rather than the other way round. You tell us your number, your date and what matters most, and we shape a plan that fits — with no pricing mazes to wade through. Start your plan or send us a message and we'll come back with a tailored quote.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to have a party at home?
faqs.a: Usually, yes — a home or condo function room removes venue-hire costs, which is often the biggest single expense. Our styling makes the space feel special without the price tag of a dedicated venue.

faqs.q: How much should I budget per child?
faqs.a: As a rough guide, catering and favours run around $15-$40 per child depending on the spread. Décor and entertainment are mostly fixed costs that don't scale much with headcount.

title: The Kids' Birthday Party Planning Checklist (Singapore, 2026)
metaDescription: A week-by-week kids' birthday party planning checklist for Singapore parents — from booking the date to the day itself, so nothing gets forgotten.
excerpt: A calm, week-by-week checklist that takes you from 'we should plan something' to a party day that runs itself.
dek: Planning a party is only stressful when it's all in your head. Here's a simple week-by-week checklist so nothing slips — and you actually enjoy the day.

sections.html:
• Set the date, rough guest count and a budget.
  • Choose a venue — home, a function room, or somewhere further afield.
  • Pick a theme your child will love.
  • If you'd like it done for you, start a party plan now to lock in your date.

• Send invitations and start collecting RSVPs.
  • Confirm the cake and any catering.
  • Book entertainment — the best acts get snapped up early.
  • Confirm décor and styling.

• Chase any missing RSVPs and finalise numbers.
  • Order party favours and confirm the running order of the day.
  • Consider a photographer so you're in the memories too.

• Confirm timings with every supplier (or let your concierge do it).
  • Prepare a simple run-of-show: arrival, activities, cake, goodbyes.
  • Charge phones and cameras; prep a small emergency kit (wipes, plasters, spare candles).

Setup happens before guests arrive, you cut the cake around the midpoint while energy is high, and everything is cleared afterwards. If we're running your party, that's exactly how it goes — you stay with your child and your guests while we handle the rest. Plan your party and we'll build the whole timeline for you.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I start planning?
faqs.a: Six to eight weeks is comfortable and gives you the best choice of dates, entertainers and styling. We can often help on much shorter notice too — just ask.

faqs.q: What's the ideal party length for young children?
faqs.a: Two hours is the sweet spot for most young children — long enough for cake and activities, short enough to end before anyone melts down.

title: How Much Does Face Painting Cost for a Kids' Party in Singapore? (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: A 2026 price guide to face painting for kids' parties in Singapore — solo freelancer vs. agency rates, per-hour pricing, what's included, and how to get good value.
excerpt: A realistic 2026 price guide to face painting for a kids' party in Singapore — solo artist vs. agency rates, what's included, and how to budget for guest count.
dek: Solo freelancer or agency, per-hour or per-package — here's what face painting actually costs for a kids' party in Singapore, and how to get real value for your money.

sections.html: Face painting for a kids' party in Singapore typically costs $150–$380 for a single booked session, depending on whether you go with a solo freelance artist or book through an agency or concierge, how long you need the artist on-site, and how many children are on your guest list. For context on how this fits your overall spend, see our guide to overall kids' party costs in Singapore — face painting is usually one line item within a broader entertainment budget.

sections.h2: Solo freelancer vs. agency or team booking
sections.html:
A solo freelance face painter found through classifieds or social media often charges $100–$180 per hour, which can look like the cheapest option on paper. The trade-off is reliability: if they fall sick, get stuck in traffic, or double-book, you have no backup and no one coordinating them with the rest of your day.

Booking through an agency or a concierge like OurKampung's face painting service usually runs a little higher — think $180–$380 for a coordinated session — but you're paying for a vetted artist, a backup plan if something goes wrong, and someone who briefs the painter on your timing and theme so they show up ready to go rather than needing directions on arrival.

Most face painters price one of two ways. Per-hour is straightforward — you pay for however long they're on-site, usually with a one-hour minimum. Per-package bundles a fixed block (commonly 1–1.5 hours) with setup and breakdown included, which is easier to budget against and is how most agency bookings work. A few extras to watch for: a travel or transport fee of roughly $20–$40 depending on your location, and a premium of 10–20% for weekend or public holiday slots, since that's when demand is highest.

sections.h2: How guest count and party duration affect the price
sections.html: One artist typically manages around 10–15 children per hour, depending on how detailed the designs are. If you've got a guest list of 30 or more young children, a single one-hour slot will leave a long queue and cranky kids waiting — you'll want either a longer booking or a second artist, both of which raise the cost. Most parties we help plan book 1 to 1.5 hours of face painting as one component of a two-hour celebration, which comfortably covers 15–20 children without anyone missing out on cake or games.

sections.h2: What's usually included and what costs extra
sections.html: A standard booking typically includes the artist's time, professional cosmetic-grade paints, a set menu of designs to choose from, and basic setup and pack-down. What often costs extra: full-face designs or anything requiring more than a couple of minutes per child, add-ons like glitter or gems, sessions extended beyond the booked time, and travel to locations outside the artist's usual coverage area. It's worth confirming these details upfront rather than finding out mid-party.

A few things make a real difference to what you get for your money:

  • Book early — good artists get snapped up for weekend slots weeks in advance.
  • Keep designs simple for parties with a lot of young or shy children, so the queue keeps moving.
  • Bundle face painting with other elements of your entertainment and décor through one concierge, so timings don't clash and you're not paying separate travel fees for every vendor.
  • Ask exactly what's included before you pay a deposit — the quote should cover time, paint quality and travel with no surprises on the day.

faqs.q: Is face painting cheaper than hiring a magician?
faqs.a: Generally, yes — a face painting session typically costs less per hour than a magician, and it can run continuously in the background rather than needing a dedicated performance slot, which is why many parents choose it as their primary entertainment for younger children.

faqs.q: Do face painters charge more on weekends or public holidays?
faqs.a: Often, yes — expect a premium of roughly 10-20% for Saturday, Sunday and public holiday bookings, since that's when demand is highest. Weekday parties can sometimes secure a better rate.

title: Face Painting vs. Other Party Entertainment: Which Is Right for Your Kid's Party?
metaDescription: Comparing face painting against magicians, balloon twisters, mascots and science shows for a kids' party in Singapore — pros, cons, best ages and how to combine them on a budget.
excerpt: Face painting, a magician, a mascot, or all three? Here's how the most popular kids' party entertainment options in Singapore compare, so you can spend your budget where it counts.
dek: Every party has a finite entertainment budget. Here's an honest comparison of the most popular options in Singapore, so you can pick — or combine — the ones that suit your child's party best.

sections.html: Most parties in Singapore budget for one, maybe two, entertainment elements — spreading further usually means each one feels rushed or underwhelming. Before you book anything, it helps to know what each option is actually like in practice, not just on a vendor's price list. Here's how the most requested options compare, so you can put your budget where your child (and their guests) will feel it most.

Best for: ages 3 and up, mixed-age guest lists, parties where kids are also doing other activities.

Face painting is one of the most efficient entertainment dollars you can spend. It runs continuously rather than needing a dedicated performance slot, doubles as a take-home 'souvenir' that photographs beautifully, and gives shy or younger children a calm one-on-one moment rather than a big group show. The trade-off is queue management with a large guest list, and it lacks the single big 'wow' moment of a scheduled performance. See our face painting service for how we run it.

Best for: ages 4–10, parties with a clear program and a moment for everyone to gather.

A good magician delivers a structured, memorable centrepiece — genuine gasps and a room full of attention on one act. The trade-off is cost (usually higher per booking than face painting or balloon twisting) and the need for a proper audience setup: seating, a clear sightline, and a slot in your run-of-show where everyone's actually ready to sit still.

Best for: ages 2–8, budget-conscious parties, younger guest lists.

Balloon twisting shares a lot of face painting's strengths — it's queue-based, produces a take-home item, and works well for younger children who might not sit still for a design. It's usually priced similarly to face painting and the two are sometimes offered by the same performer, alternating or splitting a station.

Best for: theme-driven parties, younger children who love a specific character.

A costumed mascot delivers an outsized photo-op moment, especially for a strongly themed party like a superhero celebration. Appearances are usually shorter and priced higher per minute than face painting, so mascots work best as a brief highlight — a grand entrance, a group photo, a dance — rather than the entire entertainment slot.

Best for: ages 6 and up, parties that want an interactive, high-energy centrepiece.

These shows work like a scaled-down magician's slot — structured, presenter-led, and best suited to children old enough to follow along and get involved. They're a strong choice for tween birthdays where classic party games have lost their shine.

These options aren't mutually exclusive, and some of the best-loved Singapore parties combine two: face painting running quietly in the background while a magician or mascot holds the main stage for 30–45 minutes, for instance. A common and well-priced combination is face painting plus one headline act from our wider entertainment roster — you get continuous activity for the whole party plus one unforgettable moment, without paying for two full headline bookings.

As a rough guide: face painting and balloon twisting each typically run $150–$380 per session; a magician, mascot appearance or science show typically runs $300–$600 depending on length and experience. Combining two elements naturally raises your total, so it's worth deciding your must-have moment first and building around it. If you're not sure what fits your budget and guest list, tell us your numbers and we'll suggest a sensible combination.

faqs.q: Can we book both a magician and a face painter for the same party?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's a popular combination — face painting keeps children occupied throughout while the magician provides one focused performance slot. We coordinate the timing so neither competes with the other.

faqs.q: What age is too young for face painting?
faqs.a: Most artists are comfortable painting children from around age 3, once they can sit reasonably still for a couple of minutes. For younger toddlers, a simple design on the hand or arm usually works better than a full facial design.

title: Best Face Painting Designs & Themes for Kids' Parties (Singapore)
metaDescription: The most popular face painting designs for kids' parties in Singapore — animals, superheroes, princesses, unicorns and dinosaurs — plus safety notes and tips for managing the queue.
excerpt: From safari animals to unicorn horns — the most popular face painting designs for Singapore kids' parties, how to match them to your theme, and practical tips for running a smooth queue.
dek: The right design does double duty — it delights the child wearing it and ties beautifully into your party's theme. Here's how to choose well, and what to check before you book.

sections.h2: Why the design matters as much as the artist
sections.html: A skilled artist with the wrong design brief can still leave you with a party full of mismatched faces. Before you book, it's worth thinking about which design categories suit your party's theme, your guests' ages, and how many children you're expecting — because that shapes both the look and how smoothly the queue moves. Our face painting service briefs every artist on your theme in advance so this is one less thing to manage on the day.

A few categories cover the vast majority of requests at Singapore kids' parties:

  • Animals — tigers, butterflies, cats and bunnies; a natural fit for a safari or jungle theme.
  • Superheroes — masks, lightning bolts and bold colour blocks for a superhero party.
  • Princesses and fairies — glitter tiaras, floral cheeks and delicate swirls to match a princess celebration.
  • Unicorns — rainbow horns and starry cheeks, the most-requested design for unicorn parties.
  • Dinosaurs — scales, spikes and roaring mouths for a dinosaur party.

sections.h2: Simple vs. full-face designs for younger kids
sections.html: Not every child needs (or wants) a full facial design. A small cheek or temple design takes an artist roughly 2–3 minutes and suits toddlers and younger children who find it hard to sit still. A fuller design — think a complete animal muzzle or a superhero mask across the whole face — takes closer to 5–10 minutes and works best for children aged 6 and up who can hold still and actually want the bigger look. For parties with a wide age range, it's sensible to offer both and let each child choose.

sections.h2: Matching designs to your party theme
sections.html: If your party has a set theme, briefing the artist with a short shortlist beforehand — rather than leaving it open-ended — keeps the whole afternoon feeling cohesive in photos. This works even when your guest list includes children from different friend groups or households with their own favourite themes: most artists are happy to offer two or three on-theme options alongside a handful of evergreen designs like butterflies or simple animals, so nobody feels left out.

Always confirm your artist uses professional, cosmetic-grade paint rather than craft or costume paint — the difference matters for sensitive skin. Good paints are hypoallergenic, wash off easily with soap and water, and shouldn't leave any residue on clothing or bedding. If any of your guests have known skin sensitivities, mention it when booking; most artists can do a quick patch test on the wrist first, or offer a lighter design that avoids more reactive pigments.

A face painting station can become the busiest corner of the party if it isn't managed well. A few things that help: a simple design menu (even just photos on a small board) so children choose quickly rather than browsing endlessly; sticking to two or three go-to designs per age group rather than unlimited options; and scheduling the station to run alongside other activities — games, a bouncy castle, or open play — so it's never the only thing happening and the queue never becomes the whole party.

faqs.q: How long does each face painting design take?
faqs.a: A simple cheek or temple design takes around 2-3 minutes; a full-face design takes closer to 5-10 minutes. For a party of 15-20 children in a 1-1.5 hour slot, simpler designs keep the queue moving comfortably.

faqs.q: Can face paint cause allergic reactions?
faqs.a: Reactions are uncommon with professional, hypoallergenic cosmetic-grade paint, but any product applied to skin carries some risk for sensitive children. Flag known allergies when you book so the artist can patch-test or adjust the design.
